conjecture: A monad M=(M,eta,mu) on Set transfers to a comonad G on Cont by G(S,P)=(S, M o P), with counit eps backward = eta and comultiplication delta backward = mu; the three comonad laws are exactly M's three monad laws pulled back through the position-contravariance of container morphisms (counit-left <=> M right-unit; counit-right <=> M left-unit; coassociativity <=> M associativity). Dually a comonad W on Set gives a monad H(S,P)=(S, W o P) on Cont. Neil's structural why: G is the left coclosure of the substitution product <| with M in the numerator, G(S,P)={M/(S,P)}=Lan_{(S,P)} M (left Kan extension). (Neil Ghani's Ch4 item 2, email 2026-07-24.)
